A log line says which of your items it is about, and the save mark is the one every app of mine uses.

## 🎨 Design

- **The save mark is the shared one.** Every app of mine used to keep its own floppy; this is the same drawing from the same file as ArrowLoop's. Its ink was measured rather than read off the source file, which matters more than it sounds: the drawing declares a 492 square and occupies a 368.7 one inside it, so carried over unchanged the mark would have arrived at three quarters of the size of every glyph beside it. Its label panel is a hole that winds the same way as its body, so the fill rule had to survive the import as well, or the mark renders as a blank rectangle.

## ⚡ Improved

- **Every line in the activity log says which domain it belongs to** ([#200](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/200)). A line carried the item's name and nothing else, and a container and a folder set can easily share one. Somebody chasing a running backup read "Backing up HomeDVR", went to the Folders tab, and found the set of that name sitting idle with no Stop button, because it was the container of that name that was running. Working that out should not be anybody's job. The domain was in the data the whole time, since it drives the filter above the log; it just never reached the line.

  Worth saying while you are here: the Stop button sits on the card of whatever is actually running, so a container's is on the Containers tab. A card that reads "A backup is running…" is telling you something ELSE is running; the card that owns the run carries a progress bar instead.
